title: Meta launches Muse to act across email, travel, shopping and the web
friendlyTitle: Meta’s Muse agent can help with email, travel and shopping
summary: Meta is rolling out Muse in the US on iOS, Android and the web as a personal agent that can browse, fill forms, send email, book travel and make purchases after required approvals. Meta says each user receives an isolated cloud computer, with a separate Sentinel agent reviewing outbound actions and an audit trail showing what Muse has done.
friendlySummary: Muse can use a web browser and connected apps to complete tasks for you. Meta says it asks before sensitive actions, runs in a separate cloud computer and keeps a record of its work.
whyItMatters: Muse puts broad agent access into a mainstream consumer product, making permission design more important than the quality of any single answer. Anyone trying it should begin with narrow app permissions, keep confirmations on for consequential actions and review the audit trail before trusting background work.
friendlyWhyItMatters: An agent with access to email, accounts and payments can be useful but powerful. Give it only the access it needs, keep approval checks on and read its activity record.
